 A COMPANION FOR THE JOURNEY
Small steps.
Built around you.
A little structure, a little encouragement, and space to try again.
Practice with a plan
Pick a Python topic or tell LearnPath what you want to practice. Get a short explanation and an exercise at your current level.
Find your next step
A wrong answer is a starting point. Get a hint, work through the values, and try again. You can open an example solution when you’re stuck.
A pace that fits
Fresh first-attempt answers guide difficulty. LearnPath tries different explanation styles and uses your feedback to choose future lessons. Retries and revealed solutions don’t inflate your score.
Your progress, your device
Practice history stays in this browser. Export a progress file and import it on another device to continue. There are no accounts or automatic cross-device syncing.
A working prototype, with clear limits
LearnPath currently supports four beginner topics and three practice levels. Lessons are curated and exercises are generated from checked templates. The browser version uses a feedback-driven explanation policy; it does not call a language model or run arbitrary Python.
Practice estimates are guides, not formal grades or proof of learning gains. This project has not yet been evaluated in a real-student outcome study. The lesson reference links point to the official Python documentation.
Created by Mary Balemba, based on the LearnPath Colab capstone. Try it, experiment, and keep learning.


LearnPath ● One small step at a time.






YOUR LEARNING SPACE
Make yourself at home.
No account or personal information needed. A nickname is enough.
Take your progress with you
Progress is saved in this browser. To switch devices, export a file here, then import it on your other device.
Privacy & starting fresh
LearnPath stores your nickname, exercises, explanation feedback and recent practice history in local browser storage. Your practice data is not sent to a learning server. Hosting may process standard access logs. Clearing browser data can remove your progress; keep an export if you want a backup.
An imported file replaces this browser’s current progress. Export first if you want to keep it. Anyone using this browser can access its saved profile.


Keep it to one expression.
Use the values in your exercise. The tutor calculates the result of your expression; you don’t need to write a full program.
a + bAdd two valuesscore >= pass_markCompare two valuessum(range(n))Add a bounded rangesum(items) // len(items)Find an integer average1 if score >= pass_mark else 0Choose between two values
Supported: whole numbers, True/False, given variables, short lists, + − * // %, comparisons, conditional expressions, sum, len and range. Imports, indexing, decimals, strings, powers, assignments, full loops and file/network access are not supported.
